title: Bundle entitlement and copy canvas
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working canvas to converge on: (1) which product bundles / entitlements we will publish to cloud catalogs and channel portals, (2) the exact short/long copy variants for tile + listing assets, and (3) a minimal acceptance checklist (legal, billing, infra) that must be cleared before publish. This is intentionally lightweight — use as a single source for engineers, GTM, and legal to iterate together.

Current focus: 3 sample bundles for initial channel launch (EMEA first pass):
- Core-API (hosted inference) — baseline per-token plan, aimed at dev/test workloads.
- Dedicated-Reserve (reserved capacity) — 24/7 dedicated pool + SLA; target mid-market accounts.
- Private-Edge (VPC/on-prem) — air-gapped/private instance offering for regulated customers.

Tile and listing copy (short -> medium -> long). Use these variants by channel constraints (50 chars, 150 chars, 300+ chars).
1) Core-API
  - 50-char: "Redwood Core API — fast hosted LLM inference"
  - 150-char: "Pay-as-you-go hosted inference with predictable latency and dev-friendly SDKs. Ideal for prototypes and small apps; built-in caching and streaming."
  - 300-char: "Redwood Core API gives developers low-friction access to high-performance LLM inference. Get predictable per-token economics, streaming responses, and integrations for chat, embeddings, and reranking. Start with free credits and scale to production without re-architecting your client code."

2) Dedicated-Reserve
  - 50-char: "Dedicated capacity with SLA and scale"
  - 150-char: "Reserved GPU pools with latency SLOs, autoscaling policies, and private data isolation. Designed for production apps that need consistent throughput and compliance controls."
  - 300-char: "Reserved capacity from Redwood provides enterprise-grade inference with predictable throughput and cost. Configure autoscaling, burst capacity, and private network isolation. Includes rollout controls, model pinning, and priority routing — all backed by measurable SLAs and support for on-call escalation."

3) Private-Edge
  - 50-char: "On-prem / VPC inference for regulated workloads"
  - 150-char: "Full private deployment option: customer-managed network, optional air-gapped install, and KMS/HSM integrations. For teams requiring strict data residency and audit controls."
  - 300-char: "Private-Edge enables enterprise customers to run Redwood’s inference runtime inside their VPC or on-prem cages. Offers encrypted storage, KMS/HSM key control, audit logging, and support for disconnected installations. Ideal for regulated industries where data cannot leave the customer boundary — includes deployment playbooks and optional professional services."

Hero bullets (for listing tile):
- High-throughput inference optimized for GPUs
- Predictable economics: batching and cache-aware routing
- Model versioning + A/B rollouts out of the box
- Enterprise controls: audit logs, KMS, and network isolation

Asset mapping (what we need per bundle):
- Short title (<=50 chars)
- 150-char description
- 300+ char description / product summary
- 3–5 bullet highlights (marketing)
- 2–3 technical callouts (latency SLOs, supported models, API endpoints)
- Pricing snippet (example SKUs and units)
- Legal & SSPL notes (if applicable)
- Logo/thumbnail (svg/png)

Acceptance checklist (minimal gates before publish):
- Copy signoff: GTM product manager + solutions engineer (names below)
- Legal review: licensing and data residency statement cleared
- Billing mapping: SKU created in billing system and mapped to product codes (cloud vendor)
- Security review: KMS/HSM wording validated, required SOC/IS certifications called out
- Tech smoke test: demo provisioning and end-to-end purchase flow validated in staging catalog
- Support readiness: runbook + escalation path documented for first 30 days

Owner matrix (quick):
- GTM lead: Aisha Patel (owner of copy and readiness)
- Solutions engineering: Marco Ruiz (technical acceptance)
- Legal counsel: Priya Sethi (T&C and SSPL check)
- Billing: Lee Wong (SKU and cloud mapping)
- Launch ops: Sofia Andersson (assets upload + catalog orchestration)

Open decisions / questions:
1) Pricing unit for Dedicated-Reserve — monthly seat vs vGPU-hour? (Marco to propose by 2026-03-17)
2) Should Core-API tile emphasize "free credits" or "pay-as-you-go" first in cloud catalog short title? GTM preference needed.
3) Private-Edge licensing: include a separate enterprise license line or roll into a professional services SKU? Legal to recommend.

Copy notes for channel-specific constraints:
- AWS: titles limited to ~120 chars in one field; include SKU in the description body. Avoid external links in the short description.
- Azure: requires explicit data residency options to be listed for each SKU. Include region availability matrix as a separate CSV.
- GCP: requires billing descriptor and authorized seller information for co-sell bundles.

Examples of billing mapping (sketch):
- CORE-BASE: per-1k-token unit; monthly aggregated metering
- DED-4: reserved 4 vGPU equivalent; monthly commitment SKU + burst overage token rate
- PE-ONPREM: one-time platform license (yearly maintenance) + optional managed-support SKU

Legal copy snippets (draft language to iterate):
- Data handling: "Customer data processed by Redwood for inference is retained only as necessary for operation and debugging, subject to the customer’s retention policy configured in the Console. See full DPA and Data Residency Addendum."
- Acceptable use: short AUP pointer (link placeholder) + requirement for model usage labels when publishing results externally.

Operational playbook pointers (to flesh out in staging):
- Staging catalog upload: create draft tile, attach thumbnails, short + long descriptions, tags, SKUs.
- Test purchase: simulate purchase and confirm provisioning and email notifications.
- Post-publish audit: 48hr health check (latency, error rates) and 7-day customer outreach plan for early adopters.

Unresolved risks and mitigations:
- Risk: billing SKU misalignment across clouds -> Mitigation: create canonical SKU matrix and have billing owner (Lee) sign-off one week prior to publish.
- Risk: copy rejected by marketplace compliance -> Mitigation: run copy through vendor policy checklist and keep alternative wording ready.

Short-term next steps (owners + ETA):
- Finalize pricing model for Dedicated-Reserve (Marco) — due 2026-03-17
- Legal draft for Private-Edge licensing (Priya) — due 2026-03-20
- Produce tile art and thumbnails (Sofia) — first pass by 2026-03-15
- Run one end-to-end test publish to staging for AWS (Lee + Marco) — by 2026-03-22

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider a multi-tenant starter pack that bundles Core-API + limited Dedicated burst credits — might help conversion from free credits.
- Flag: do we need a separate "training data" statement for model-eval endpoints? Pull in research/ops guidance.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-5243 (catalog readiness checklist)
- Jira epic: JIRA-GB-1127 (catalog launch epic)
- Asset repo: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets (PR 87 for first thumbnails)

End of draft — use this canvas to iterate. Add comments inline or update the acceptance checklist as you validate pieces.

-- Aisha
